With Discourse's rest serializer behavior, `embed: :ids` emits an `embeddable_host_ids` array on the embedding object AND side-loads the serialized host records in the same payload, which is exactly what the diff's `_hydrateEmbedded` change supports (`const m = /(.+)\_id(s?)$/` handling plural ids via `_lookupSubType`). The finding's core claim that host objects are not included in the payload is contradicted by this standard rest_serializer side-loading mechanism and by the diff's store.js changes that were written to consume precisely this pattern.

judged_text: [Medium/bug] app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:4 — `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` side-loads only IDs and does not include the host objects in the payload, so the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` cannot resolve them; `embedding.embeddable_hosts` will not be usable records and the host table in embedding.hbs won't render properly

adjudication.rationale: In this codebase, `has_many ..., embed: :ids` is used to *sideloadd* the full associated objects alongside an `*_ids` field. The diff also updates the JS store hydration to handle plural `*_ids` keys (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` in `store.js.es6`) by mapping them into `obj[pluralize(subType)]` (e.g. `embeddable_host_ids` -> `embeddable_hosts`) and resolving them from the sideloaded root collection. So `embedding.embeddable_hosts` should be usable records and the table can render; the finding incorrectly assumes only IDs are sent with no sideloaded objects.
